dataStory.t: Leaps out of reach and lands on the next turn
Reveals a foe's HP and weaknesses
Reveals every foe's HP and weaknesses
Pushes back every foe's turn (half as far for bosses)
Restores everyone to at least 60% HP
Fully heals and cures the party
Always lands as a weakness (breaks Poise)
Stronger the more HP you have lost
Stronger the fuller the Afterglow gauge
Cuts a quarter of current HP (8% against bosses)
Heals the party 25% and restores 10% MP
Halves damage until your next turn
Quick: your next turn comes sooner
Heavy: your next turn comes later
Afterglow gain +25%. Once per battle, survive a lethal blow at 1 HP.
Daughter of the Keeper of Lanternfall. Reads every book the tide brings in. Wants, more than anything, to leave.
Healing on allies below 30% HP is 50% stronger.
Wren's best friend since before either could walk. Herbalist's apprentice. Has a plan for everything, including the plan failing.
Once per battle, take a lethal blow meant for an ally.
Squire of the Dawnguard, exiled to Lanternfall after he froze during his knighting trial. Loud. Kind. Certain he is a coward.
Attacks may inflict a random ailment. Immune to Doom.
Washed ashore in a storm with no memory and a Crest no Lantern has ever seen.
Aurenne street kid. Steals for a living, lies for fun, and would die before admitting he's eleven.
1 in 6 chance a skill costs no MP and hits twice as hard.
Captain of the airship Halcyon. Smuggler, gambler, Dawnguard deserter. Owes everyone money, including himself.
s lemonade, for Bess. It has been on its way for forty years.
A splinter of the broken sun that learned to walk. It is warm, and it is not kind.
The Choir's hounds, bred in the Spire's light. They cast no shadow at all.
An eye of noon, floating. Looking at it is like looking at the sun, which nobody has done for a year.
The Spire's guard. They have been promised the best day of their lives, as soon as their shift ends.
A hymn given wings. It heals whatever stands between it and you.
Keeper of the Spire's back door. He has turned away four hundred pilgrims and remembers every face.
Armor wound like a clock. It stops when it is struck — and so, for a moment, do you.
A moment that never ended, drifting. Cold as an afternoon that will not let you go home.
They eat memories the way other moths eat coats. The Spire is a feast.
They practice the Vespersong in shifts. Somebody, somewhere in the Spire, is always singing it.
The Spire's keeper of hours. It has only ever counted to twelve, and it has done so for forty years.
"Lovely day for it!" it says, and smiles, and smiles, and comes for your throat.
A festival lantern that drifted loose. The candle inside has burned for forty years and never got any shorter.
Somebody's dog, remembered as a very good dog. Remembered a little too hard.
"Welcome to the Festival of the Long Light. Enjoy the day." Forever.
She has been dancing round the maypole since before your parents were born. She would love you to join in.
Mercy's congregation. They sing for her because she promised them they would never have to stop.
Evernoon's warden. She believes that a day which never ends cannot hurt anyone. She has never once been told no and believed it.
Where Evernoon comes apart, the Gloam comes in. It wears whatever it finds.
Its strings are cut. Its sentence is unfinished. It is very, very angry about both.
Every sentence Evernoon never finished, knotted together into something that wants, very badly, to be heard.
The Warden's clock-face cracks — its hands spin all the way back!
s hand moves. It is ${HOURS[c.m.hour]} o
"NOON." Every bell in Evernoon rings at once.
Mercy lets down her hood. "You will not take her. You will not take ANY of them." She sings the Vespersong.
Hush. Be still. Be still forever."
"Rest now." A lullaby — and under it, the bells of Evernoon begin to swing...
"—IT!" A hundred mouths finish the sentence at once.
It begins to forget its own shape. Light pours through the gaps — light no longer heals it!
A puppet tears loose from its body and staggers forward!
s cutlass, from the wreck of the Gull's Return. Still sharp. He oiled it every Sunday.
s sigil, found lashed to your father's boat with a Keeper's knot.
s log. The last page is addressed to someone.
It swims through the glass dunes the way an eel swims through weed. The dunes are in the sky now. It has not noticed.
A memory of water seen by someone dying of thirst.
Blindfolded and singing one note. Tamsin's acolytes sang the Dawnsong with their eyes covered, so they would hear it better.
Its shell is fused desert glass. Hit it hard enough and it rings.
What remains of Keeper Tamsin: a choir of blindfolded voices singing so loudly they cannot hear the world end.
One voice of many. It sings harmony to a song no one else can hear.
The monks of Frosthollow kept a silent vigil. Some of them are still keeping it.
It hunts by the sound of chattering teeth.
The avalanche that killed Brother Halvard, gathered up and given a grudge.
A slope of snow that remembers falling.
Brother Halvard, kneeling in the snow, apologizing to a mountain. He has been at it for a year.
Mirefen's healers used leeches. The leeches have started using the healers.
Lives in the stilts. Bites the ankles of anyone who stands still too long.
It waits under the boardwalks for the rot to finish its work.
Mother Osk, who nursed her village through the rot and could not stop when they died. She is still nursing.
It cries like a feverish child. Do not listen too closely.
An oak that was old when Aurenne was a village. It is very tired of standing.
More thorn than dog, now. It still wags.
Drawn to the last light in any room. Drinks it.
Verdance's fairies were said to live as long as a summer. Summer ended.
Elowen, the oldest Keeper, who would not fade. She drank the forest to stay in bloom.
Stormcrown's riders flew drakes like these. The drakes kept flying.
It dives with the lightning, never before it.
Vasha's honor guard. The armor stands its watch with nothing inside.
A spark that got lost on the way down and decided to stay.
Ardent Vasha, who gave the Hierophant her light because he asked so kindly. She is still announcing his coming.
Cassian's chosen. They took the Vesper oath: to hold the moment, whatever it costs.
The last of Garrick's men. They stayed because he stayed.
They sing the Vespersong in rounds, to keep the moment warm.
A bell from the City of Bells, given legs and told to toll for the end of time.
Garrick's second. He has polished the same breastplate every morning for a year, because no one told him to stop.
Head of the Dawnguard and Cassian's sword. He has seen the world broken, and would rather it frozen.
No title now. No soldiers. Just a man with a sword, and another man with a sword.
He is bleeding. So is Bram. Neither of them is sitting down.
Something that happened here, once, on an ordinary day. It wants to happen again.
Lanternfall's gulls were always bold. They are bolder dead.
Everything the sea took from Lanternfall, wound together and come home.
It has circled the Lantern for a year. It has never once thought of leaving.
You fought it on the night Sable washed ashore. It remembers you. You were so much smaller.
A little of the light she could not let go of.
Ysolde Halloway, Keeper of Lanternfall, still holding the last light so her daughter can reach the boat.
It walked the sea floor its whole life. The floor is in the sky now. It keeps walking.
It drifts above the reef, pulsing like a slow heart.
It nests in the ribs of drowned ships.
The storm that took Edrin Halloway, remembered by the sea it happened in.
A fever that broke, a year too late.
Clean sheets. Folded corners. Something still lying in them.
Every long night on every ward, given a voice. It sounds exactly like Ilse on her worst day.
Every knight who ever stood the vigil here left a little of themselves in the stone. It stands up to see if you are worthy.
The squires who failed the vigil. They are not angry. Only cold.
